classification.difficultyReason: Extend standard trigonometric sketches to negative angles, locating quadrantal values and two tangent asymptotes and drawing the three increasing tangent branches on the specified interval.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of the following in the domain $x\in[-\pi,\pi]$.

answer.short: A smooth sine curve through $(-\pi,0)$, $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$ and $(\pi,0)$.
answer.worked: Plot the five key points $(-\pi,0)$, $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$ and $(\pi,0)$. Join them smoothly, with a minimum at $(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1)$ and a maximum at $(\frac{\pi}{2},1)$.

spec.description: Sine curve over a full turn centred on the origin.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed sketch with extrema and horizontal positions labelled.

answer.short: A smooth cosine curve through $(-\pi,-1)$, $(-\frac{\pi}{2},0)$, $(0,1)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},0)$ and $(\pi,-1)$.
answer.worked: Plot the five key points $(-\pi,-1)$, $(-\frac{\pi}{2},0)$, $(0,1)$, $(\frac{\pi}{2},0)$ and $(\pi,-1)$. Join them with a smooth curve symmetric about the vertical axis, with maximum $(0,1)$.

spec.description: Cosine curve symmetric about the vertical axis over the requested interval.

answer.short: Three increasing branches; zeros at $x=-\pi,0,\pi$ and vertical asymptotes at $x=-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}$.
answer.worked: Mark the zeros at $(-\pi,0)$, $(0,0)$ and $(\pi,0)$. Draw vertical asymptotes at $x=-\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Draw increasing branches on each interval: each approaches $+\infty$ on the left of an asymptote and $-\infty$ on its right.

spec.description: Three increasing tangent branches and two dashed vertical asymptotes.
spec.mathematics: y=tan x on [-pi,pi], excluding -pi/2 and pi/2.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed sketch with asymptote positions and endpoints labelled.
